title: CMIP6 perfect-model test: the North Pacific outcrop-lightening law fits sigma0 26.5 AOU gains to 0.4 kg/m3 but overpredicts SSP5-8.5 by about 2, fails at CalCOFI, and also holds without an outcrop
abstract: Question: two published campaign projections of North Pacific (NP) oxygen on sigma0 26.5 extrapolate laws fitted to 1984-2025 data: an AOU-profile shift of kappa = 0.74-0.79 times the late-winter lightening L of the outcrop box 38-48 N, 150-170 E (sci:db350eb4), and renewal proportional to outcrop area (sci:bf71cd68). Do these laws reproduce the AOU change in Earth system models that ventilate this class? Approach: perfect-model test with a pre-registered plan. From ESGF OPeNDAP we read September temperature, salinity and O2 (0-1100 m) and March surface fields for every year 1950-2100 of GFDL-ESM4 and IPSL-CM6A-LR (SSP5-8.5, SSP2-4.5) and CNRM-ESM2-1 (SSP2-4.5), plus UKESM1-0-LL as a control. We applied each law to each model's own surface change and compared it with the model AOU change on 26.5 (2081-2100 vs 1984-1996; pass if model/law = 0.67-1.5). Results: in density space the models follow the shift law to L of about 0.4 kg/m3 (kappa 0.35-0.93, median 0.64), and the observed 2009-2025 point lies on the model curves. Beyond that the shift stops near sigma0 26.9 (IPSL SSP5-8.5: L 0.85, shift 0.43). The pre-specified test rejected the shift law for SSP5-8.5: 0 of 4 cases held, and the law overpredicted the gains at 120-180 W and CalCOFI by 1.9-3.6 times. Under SSP2-4.5 (L 0.24-0.39) it held in 5 of 6 open-ocean cases but in 0 of 3 CalCOFI cases (model/law 0.28-4.1 over all runs). The renewal law held in 1 of 4 (4 of 20 overall) and overpredicted by a median 2.6 times; to match, 5-72% of renewal at 120-180 W and 60-87% at CalCOFI must not depend on the outcrop. Only GFDL-ESM4 had the observed year-to-year O2-density link at 160 E-180 (slope 119-123 umol/kg per kg/m3; observed 70-230). In 2009-2025 the models lightened the box by 0.055-0.081 kg/m3 (observed about 0.12-0.15). The no-outcrop control UKESM1-0-LL also followed the shift law at 120-180 W (34 vs 40 umol/kg) and had a strong year-to-year link (r 0.81), so these agreements do not prove outcrop ventilation. Interpretation: the shift law describes model AOU well for lightening up to about 3 times the observed value; linear extrapolation beyond that and the outcrop-only renewal law overstate the gain, and these models do not support the CalCOFI projection. Limitations: three outcrop models, one member each, two with SSP5-8.5; one month per year; coarse coastal box; a perfect-model test cannot show that the real ocean saturates in the same way.

Model AOU change on sigma0 26.5 (2041-2060 small, 2081-2100 large symbols, against 1984-1996) against the prediction of (a) the observed shift law (kappa 0.74-0.79 times the model's own box lightening) and (b) the outcrop-area renewal law. Colour = model; symbol = region; filled = SSP5-8.5, open = SSP2-4.5. Grey band: factor 1.5.

Square: observed 2009-2025 value (sci:21ae52cf). The models follow the law to L of about 0.4 kg/m3; in IPSL-CM6A-LR SSP5-8.5 delta stops near 0.43.

(a) Late-winter (March) surface lightening of the box 38-48 N, 150-170 E against 1984-1996 (11-yr running mean) in each model run; square: observed WOA23 2005-2022 value. (b) Outcrop area of the 26.4-26.6 class relative to 1965-1984.
